_comment: Durable source of truth for hand-researched estimates, alongside companies.json for the universe. These rows are the most expensive artifact in the project — each one is a human reading filings — and catalyst.db is gitignored and regenerable, so they must live here or a rebuild destroys them. Every row needs a filing-backed basis citing accession numbers; see the verification standard in HANDOFF.md. NOTE the classifier consequence: a buildout_estimates p50 overrides streak-based maturity in stages.py — past that date a company with revenue is stage 5 regardless of momentum.

catalyst_estimates.basis: Starlab commercial space station (Voyager-led JV; Airbus/Mitsubishi/MDA/Palantir partners). Per 10-K filed 2026-03-10 (accn 0001628280-26-016543): launch anticipated 2029 on SpaceX Starship, revenue expected in first full year of operation (~2030); est. cost $2.8-3.3B vs $217.5M NASA Phase I grant ($34.3M remaining at YE2025) — bulk of funding NOT secured; CDR not yet complete; NASA Phase II CLD award not yet competed; ISS decommission 2030 sets demand timing. Catalyst = first Starlab segment revenue (segment is pre-revenue; company's D&ST segment already generates revenue). p10: on-schedule 2029 launch + first-year revenue. p50: 1.5-2.5yr slip (unfunded capex, CDR ahead, launch-vehicle dependency). p90: major slip. Conditional on program survival — Phase II loss or funding failure could remove the catalyst entirely.

FCC Lower 900 MHz rulemaking. Petition filed 2024-04-16 (15 MHz nationwide 5G NR + PNT config); still pending with NO NPRM as of 10-Q filed 2026-08-11 (accn 0001554855-26-001789); referenced in FCC PNT Notice of Inquiry 2025-03-27. Catalyst = material revenue from spectrum monetization via MNO partnership. p10: NPRM ~6mo + R&O 2027 + fast partner ramp. p50: contested R&O 2028-29 (902-928 MHz unlicensed incumbents opposed) + ~1yr to first partner revenue. p90: reconsideration/litigation drag. Dates conditional on grant — outright denial is a live risk that removes the catalyst; company itself cites 'significant regulatory uncertainty' (contingent consideration unrecognized).

buildout_estimates.basis: Starlab full operational capability (the maturity milestone, distinct from first revenue in catalyst_estimates). Sources: 10-K period 2025-12-31 (accn 0001628280-26-016543, filed 2026-03-10) and 10-Q period 2026-06-30 (accn 0001628280-26-052292, filed 2026-08-04). COMPANY POSITION: cost to design, manufacture and launch Starlab estimated at $2.8-3.3B, 'with launch anticipated in 2029 and revenue generation expected in Starlab's first full year of operation'; PDR completed January 2025; company is advancing 'through Critical Design Review toward hardware production'. ISS decommissioning in 2030 is the schedule driver. INDEPENDENT BUILD-RATE CHECK (the archetype method — spend to date vs. program cost vs. observed rate): construction in progress $37.3M at 2024-12-31, $143.9M at 2025-12-31, $193.5M at 2026-06-30. That is +$106.6M during 2025 and +$49.6M in H1 2026, i.e. a run rate near $100M/yr against a $2.8-3.3B program. Roughly 6-7% of the low-end program cost is in the ground after two years of acceleration. A 2029 launch is not reachable at the observed rate; it requires a step-change in funding. FUNDING GAP: the Nanoracks agreement's $217.5M of milestone funding is now fully drawn — 'All milestone payments have now been earned as of June 30, 2026' — and government grant assistance offset against CIP is falling ($20.3M in Q2 2025 vs $7.0M in Q2 2026). NASA Phase II CLD has not been competed yet, so the largest prospective funding source is unawarded. One launch is under commitment at $90.0M with no date given ('a future estimated launch date'). p10 2031-12-31: Phase II CLD award lands near-term and financing closes; launch near the company's 2029-2030 guidance plus roughly a year of commissioning. p50 2034-06-30: launch slips to ~2032-33 — CDR incomplete at the last filing, and >$2.5B remains to be funded against a ~$100M/yr observed build rate — with full operational capability about a year after. p90 2039-12-31: program descoped, restructured, or repeatedly delayed. ORDERING: deliberately later than this company's catalyst estimate (p50 2032-06-30) at every percentile — revenue is expected in the first full year of operation, so first revenue precedes full buildout. NOT conditional on Starlab being the sole ISS successor; a Phase II loss would push past p90 rather than merely delay.

Merlin constellation fully operational — the next discrete buildout milestone, distinct from first revenue (Satellogic already has revenue; no catalyst estimate on file). Sources: 10-K period 2025-12-31 (accn 0001874315-26-000013, filed 2026-03-19) and 10-Q period 2026-06-30 (accn 0001874315-26-000032, filed 2026-08-06). COMPANY POSITION: Merlin 'is expected to launch its first satellite, Merlin.01 in the fourth quarter of 2026, and become fully operational in the first half of 2027' — stated in the 10-K and reaffirmed verbatim in the 10-Q filed three weeks before this estimate. The 10-K adds that Merlin 'is fully funded by existing customer contracts', and a September 2022 constellation-as-a-service agreement has 'revenue on the contract expected in 2027'. THIRD-PARTY VERIFICATION (preferred over company-reported counts per CLAUDE.md): CelesTrak GP catalog queried 2026-08-28 returns 19 NUSAT-* objects with epochs of 2026-08-27/28 — exactly matching the 10-K's 'our satellite constellation consists of 19 NewSat satellites in orbit'. Highest is NUSAT-54, with gaps at 27-32, 34, 36, 43 and 46, i.e. the fleet is 19 of ~30 launched; attrition is real and the company-reported count is not inflated. (SNUSAT-2 is a separate Korean cubesat and is excluded from the count.) BUILD-RATE CHECK: 'Satellites under construction' $14.8M at 2025-12-31 -> $24.9M at 2026-06-30 (+68% in six months), and purchases of property and equipment $11.2M in H1 2026 vs $2.7M in H1 2025 (4.2x). The 10-Q states plainly: 'The Company has increased its purchases of equipment as we build our Merlin constellation.' Unlike Voyager, the observed build rate is CONSISTENT with the stated schedule and the program is funded — which is why p10 sits at the company's own date rather than well past it. COUNTERVAILING: the Q4 2026 first launch had not occurred as of this estimate and depends on a third-party launch slot; 'fully operational' for a daily global scan layer requires a constellation rather than Merlin.01 alone, so it needs multiple launches plus commissioning (the company had 'two satellites in commissioning' at 2025-12-31, so commissioning is a months-long step); and Satellogic is selling satellites OUT of the operational fleet — a $12M sovereign-defense sale of a commissioned in-orbit NewSat announced 2026-04-30, $8.3M cash received in H1 — which raises revenue while shrinking the deployed asset base ('Satellites and other equipment' fell $32.1M -> $28.4M). p10 2027-06-30: company guidance met exactly — funded, capex already accelerating. p50 2028-06-30: roughly one year of slip, the ordinary outcome when a multi-launch constellation is guided 'fully operational' two quarters after a first launch that has not yet flown. p90 2030-12-31: repeated launch slips, funding beyond existing customer contracts, or descope. CLASSIFIER NOTE: p50 is in the future, so the calendar override does not fire and the current stage is unaffected. Satellogic is NOT left-censored (stage 2-2), so unlike Voyager this row will genuinely flip it to stage 5 once 2028-06-30 passes — revisit before then rather than letting the calendar decide unattended.
